Postmortems and runbook changes must reference bundle paths.\\n\\nRunbook testing and acceptance criteria\\n\\n- Acceptance test: each runbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.\\n- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.\\n\\nEscalation and credits policy (brief)\\n\\n- If an incident leads to an SLA breach (as defined by our contracts), the SRE manager will coordinate with finance and legal on credits. Escalation to account team occurs within 60 minutes for enterprise customers.\\n\\nAppendix: quick-check triage checklist\\n\\n1) Acknowledge page and create incident channel.\\n2) Determine scope: internal-only, subset of customers, or platform-wide.\\n3) Check SLO dashboards for P99 and error rate.\\n4) Run core diagnostics (see runbook).\\n5) If containment exists, execute and mark time.\\n6) Publish status page initial message and email/Slack to account team.\\n\\nAppendix: contact matrix (example)\\n\\n- PagerDuty escalation: On-call primary -> backup -> SRE manager -> Eng Director\\n- Slack: #inc-ops (bridge), @oncall-team (escalation mentions)\\n\\nAppendix: sample runbook header (copy into top of each runbook)\\n\\nTitle: runtime-prefix-eviction-P1\\nService: redwood-runtime\\nSteward: Aisha Patel (or assigned engineer)\\nCreated: 2024-11-12\\nLast reviewed: 2025-02-12\\nChangelog:\\n- 2025-02-12: clarified eviction thresholds and added redis diagnostics\\n\\nFeedback and continued improvement\\n\\n- If you identify gaps in this policy or the runbook template, open a docs PR and tag @Runbook-Curation.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n# Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\n\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\n\nSpace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\nAuthor: Aisha Patel\n\nOwner Team: engineering\n\nStatus: published\n\nCreated At: 2024-11-12\n\nLast Updated: 2025-02-18\n\n## Reviewers\n\n- Diego Morales\n  - Priya Singh\n\n## Labels\n\n- runbook\n  - incident-ownership\n  - rotations\n  - game-day\n  - postmortem\n\n## Related Pages\n\n- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cached-kv-eviction-playbook\n  - /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024\n\nConfidentiality: internal\n\nContent: Overview\n\nPurpose: This document defines how we curate runbooks, assign incident ownership, and standardize on-call rotations, game-day exercises, postmortem output, and customer status templates. It establishes a lifecycle for runbooks (creation → review → retirement), a lightweight incident command ladder, and concrete communication templates for status page and customer notices.\n\nAudience: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners, people-ops, and incident commanders.\n\nKey definitions\n\n- Service owner: team and primary engineer responsible for the long-term health of a service (maintenance, SLOs, runbooks).\n- Incident commander (IC): temporary owner of incident coordination until handoff.\n- Operator / responder: engineer executing runbooks.\n- Runbook steward: person responsible for keeping runbooks accurate and up-to-date.\n\nRunbook lifecycle and governance\n\n1) Creation (initial authoring)\n- Required fields for each runbook: title, service, primary steward, last-reviewed, related playbooks, severity tiers covered, prerequisites, immediate containment steps, and post-incident tasks.\n- Add a short summary line at the top: single-sentence intended use.\n- Naming convention: service-action-severity (e.g., runtime-prefix-eviction-P1).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n, service, primary steward, last-reviewed, related playbooks, severity tiers covered, prerequisites, immediate containment steps, and post-incident tasks.\n- Add a short summary line at the top: single-sentence intended use.\n- Naming convention: service-action-severity (e.g., runtime-prefix-eviction-P1).\n\n2) Review cadence\n- All runbooks must be reviewed at least once every 90 days. Ownership rotates quarterly with the service squad.\n- Review checklist: verify commands, confirm contact names, run the smoke checks, and validate any TTL/threshold values.\n\n3) Versioning and change history\n- Inline header must include: steward, created_at, last_updated, changelog (bullet of top 3 changes).\n- For substantive changes (commands/scripts updated, thresholds changed), create a pull request in the docs repo and request at least one reviewer from an adjacent team.\n\n4) Retirement\n- If a runbook is unused for 12+ months and tests fail, flag for retirement. Keep an archive list with rationale and last-tested date.\n\nRunbook content standard (template)\n\n- Title: short descriptive name\n- Summary: one-sentence purpose\n- Service(s) affected: list\n- Severity mapping: P1/P2/P3 descriptions for this runbook\n- Preconditions: required credentials, network access, tooling (kubectl, pdctl, ssh)\n- Initial detection: alert names and metrics that trigger use (SLO threshold names)\n- Immediate containment steps (ordered, numbered)\n- Diagnostics (commands and expected outputs)\n- Escalation matrix: who to call at 0/15/30/60 minutes\n- Rollforward/rollback instructions (if applicable)\n- Post-incident checklist: evidence to collect, owners for RCA actions, timeline capture notes\n- Test plan: how to safely exercise this runbook in game days\n\nExample diagnostics snippets",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\nation matrix: who to call at 0/15/30/60 minutes\n- Rollforward/rollback instructions (if applicable)\n- Post-incident checklist: evidence to collect, owners for RCA actions, timeline capture notes\n- Test plan: how to safely exercise this runbook in game days\n\nExample diagnostics snippets\n\n- Check runtime pod health:\n  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide\n- Inspect logs for OOMKill or liveness probes:\n  kubectl -n redwood logs [pod] --since=10m | grep -E \"OOMKilled|liveness probe failed\"\n- Check queue depth (Redis):\n  redis-cli -h redis-svc info | grep \"instantaneous_ops_per_sec\"\n\nIncident ownership ladder\n\n- T0 (First 10 minutes): Pager recipient acknowledges and triages. If obvious containment step exists, operator executes it.\n- T10 (10–30 minutes): Incident Commander (IC) appointed by on-call rotation. IC declares impact and channels (bridge + Slack channel) and assigns roles: comms, triage lead, and mitigation lead.\n- T30 (30–90 minutes): Service owner / engineering lead joins. IC maintains timeline and coordinates cross-team dependencies.\n- T90+: If unresolved, escalate to SRE manager and Platform Eng lead; consider customer notifications and credits policy.\n\nSLO & severity mapping examples (illustrative)\n\n- P99 latency SLO: <= 150 ms for request-path /v1/generate (global).\n- Error rate SLO: 0.02 (2%) errors per 1m window.\n- Severity mapping:\n  - Sev1 / P1: Revenue-impacting, >50% customers affected, SLO broken for >10 minutes.\n  - Sev2 / P2: Significant degradation for subset of customers, SLO degraded but not fully broken.\n  - Sev3 / P3: Minor customer impact, isolated errors or performance blips.\n\nOn-call rotation stewardship",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n>50% customers affected, SLO broken for >10 minutes.\n  - Sev2 / P2: Significant degradation for subset of customers, SLO degraded but not fully broken.\n  - Sev3 / P3: Minor customer impact, isolated errors or performance blips.\n\nOn-call rotation stewardship\n\n- Rotation length: 1 week. Primary on-call with a secondary backup.\n- Handoff checklist (to be completed in PagerDuty notes & Slack):\n  1) Current ongoing incidents and bridge links\n  2) Outstanding action items requiring follow-up\n  3) Recent runbook changes or flaky alerts\n  4) Contactable escalations and out-of-hours numbers\n- Fairness rules: no more than 2 weekend rotations per quarter; swaps must be logged and approved by the manager.\n- Shadowing: new on-call engineers must shadow 2 rotations and complete the on-call checklist exercise in a game day within first 30 days.\n\nGame day (exercise) playbook\n\nPurpose: validate runbooks, surface gaps in escalations, exercise comms and status page flows.\n\nPlanning timeline:\n- T-21 days: propose scenario and get approval from relevant service owner and SRE lead.\n- T-7 days: announce to org with scope and blackout windows.\n- T-0: execute exercise in staging or canary region.\n- T+1 day: publish game day findings and action items.\n\nSample game day scenario (KV cache eviction storm):\n- Objective: ensure runbook steps contain safe containment for high-throughput prefix-cache misses.\n- Roles: IC (SRE on call), operator (service on call), comms (product liaison), observer (engineering steward).\n- Exercises:\n  1) Trigger synthetic traffic to simulate cache thundering (lower QPS to safe window first).\n  2) Follow runbook: rollback deploy, throttle traffic, enable fallback model variant.\n  3) Evaluate status page message dissemination and internal bridging.\n\nPostmortem and RCA standard",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n- Exercises:\n  1) Trigger synthetic traffic to simulate cache thundering (lower QPS to safe window first).\n  2) Follow runbook: rollback deploy, throttle traffic, enable fallback model variant.\n  3) Evaluate status page message dissemination and internal bridging.\n\nPostmortem and RCA standard\n\n- When to write: all P1 incidents and either a P2 with customer impact or any incident that required multi-team coordination.\n- Template (must be filled):\n  - Title: incident-service-date-impact\n  - Summary: 2–4 sentence summary\n  - Impact: timeline of customer-facing symptoms, number of affected customers, duration\n  - Root cause analysis: facts, timeline, gap analysis (tools, people, process)\n  - Remediation actions: owner, ETA, verification steps\n  - Preventative actions: what will change in monitoring, runbook, or code\n  - Postmortem severity and lessons learned\n  - Signal evidence: links to logs, graph snapshots, and saved traces\n- Postmortem review: present to incident review board within 5 business days. Action items must have owners & due dates.\n\nStatus page and customer comms templates\n\n- Principles: be timely, concise, factual, and avoid speculation. Provide regular cadence updates (every 30–60 minutes for P1 until mitigation).\n\nTemplate: Major Outage (P1)\n- Title: [Major Outage] Service name — Degraded / Unavailable\n- Initial post (15 min): We are investigating reports of degraded performance for the /v1/generate endpoint. Impact: some customers may see increased latency or errors. We are actively investigating and have started mitigation actions. Next update: in 30 minutes.\n- Follow-up post (30 min): Root cause update or actions taken (e.g., \"We identified a KV cache thundering event caused by recent rollout X; rolling back to previous model variant and throttling upstream traffic.\")\n- Restore post: Confirm restoration, provide ETA for full verification, and link to postmortem when available.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\npost (30 min): Root cause update or actions taken (e.g., \"We identified a KV cache thundering event caused by recent rollout X; rolling back to previous model variant and throttling upstream traffic.\")\n- Restore post: Confirm restoration, provide ETA for full verification, and link to postmortem when available.\n\nTemplate: Degraded Performance (P2)\n- Title: [Degraded Performance] Service name — Elevated error rate\n- Initial post: We are seeing an elevated error rate on request-path X affecting a subset of customers. Engineers are investigating. If you are experiencing issues, please contact support with request ID. Next update: 60 minutes.\n\nCustomer-facing email snippet (for enterprise customers)\n\nSubject: Incident update — [Service] — {Short description}\nBody:\nHello {CustomerName},\n\nWe are writing to update you about an incident affecting {Service}. Impact: {brief impact summary}. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue and we anticipate a resolution within {ETA}. We will provide another update at {time}.\n\nIf you have urgent concerns, reply to this email or contact your account team.\n\nSincerely,\nRedwood Inference Support (on-call team)\n\nOperational metrics & evidence collection\n\n- Minimum evidence to collect during incident: start/end time, commands run and outputs, screenshots of monitoring graphs, key log snippets, and affected customer IDs. Save snapshots to incident bundle in S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/{incident-id}/.\n- Retention: incident bundles retained for 24 months. Postmortems and runbook changes must reference bundle paths.\n\nRunbook testing and acceptance criteria\n\n- Acceptance test: each runbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.\n- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.\n\nEscalation and credits policy (brief)",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\nrunbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.\n- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.\n\nEscalation and credits policy (brief)\n\n- If an incident leads to an SLA breach (as defined by our contracts), the SRE manager will coordinate with finance and legal on credits. Escalation to account team occurs within 60 minutes for enterprise customers.\n\nAppendix: quick-check triage checklist\n\n1) Acknowledge page and create incident channel.\n2) Determine scope: internal-only, subset of customers, or platform-wide.\n3) Check SLO dashboards for P99 and error rate.\n4) Run core diagnostics (see runbook).\n5) If containment exists, execute and mark time.\n6) Publish status page initial message and email/Slack to account team.\n\nAppendix: contact matrix (example)\n\n- PagerDuty escalation: On-call primary -> backup -> SRE manager -> Eng Director\n- Slack: #inc-ops (bridge), @oncall-team (escalation mentions)\n\nAppendix: sample runbook header (copy into top of each runbook)\n\nTitle: runtime-prefix-eviction-P1\nService: redwood-runtime\nSteward: Aisha Patel (or assigned engineer)\nCreated: 2024-11-12\nLast reviewed: 2025-02-12\nChangelog:\n- 2025-02-12: clarified eviction thresholds and added redis diagnostics\n\nFeedback and continued improvement\n\n- If you identify gaps in this policy or the runbook template, open a docs PR and tag @Runbook-Curation. We will incorporate changes monthly and publish a changelog.\n\nRelated resources\n\n- SLO dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/slo\n- Incident bundle S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/\n- Runbook repo: https://git.internal.redwood/runbooks\n\nApproved by: SRE Lead (Diego Morales), Platform Eng Lead (Priya Singh)\n\nTitle Field Name: title",

{
  "title": "Runbook Curation and Incident Ownership Guidelines",
  "space": "oncall-and-incident-response",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-12",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-18",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Morales",
    "Priya Singh"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "runbook",
    "incident-ownership",
    "rotations",
    "game-day",
    "postmortem"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/cached-kv-eviction-playbook",
    "/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Overview

Purpose: This document defines how we curate runbooks, assign incident ownership, and standardize on-call rotations, game-day exercises, postmortem output, and customer status templates. It establishes a lifecycle for runbooks (creation → review → retirement), a lightweight incident command ladder, and concrete communication templates for status page and customer notices.

Audience: on-call engineers, SREs, service owners, people-ops, and incident commanders.

Key definitions

- Service owner: team and primary engineer responsible for the long-term health of a service (maintenance, SLOs, runbooks).
- Incident commander (IC): temporary owner of incident coordination until handoff.
- Operator / responder: engineer executing runbooks.
- Runbook steward: person responsible for keeping runbooks accurate and up-to-date.

Runbook lifecycle and governance

1) Creation (initial authoring)
- Required fields for each runbook: title, service, primary steward, last-reviewed, related playbooks, severity tiers covered, prerequisites, immediate containment steps, and post-incident tasks.
- Add a short summary line at the top: single-sentence intended use.
- Naming convention: service-action-severity (e.g., runtime-prefix-eviction-P1).

2) Review cadence
- All runbooks must be reviewed at least once every 90 days. Ownership rotates quarterly with the service squad.
- Review checklist: verify commands, confirm contact names, run the smoke checks, and validate any TTL/threshold values.

3) Versioning and change history
- Inline header must include: steward, created_at, last_updated, changelog (bullet of top 3 changes).
- For substantive changes (commands/scripts updated, thresholds changed), create a pull request in the docs repo and request at least one reviewer from an adjacent team.

4) Retirement
- If a runbook is unused for 12+ months and tests fail, flag for retirement. Keep an archive list with rationale and last-tested date.

Runbook content standard (template)

- Title: short descriptive name
- Summary: one-sentence purpose
- Service(s) affected: list
- Severity mapping: P1/P2/P3 descriptions for this runbook
- Preconditions: required credentials, network access, tooling (kubectl, pdctl, ssh)
- Initial detection: alert names and metrics that trigger use (SLO threshold names)
- Immediate containment steps (ordered, numbered)
- Diagnostics (commands and expected outputs)
- Escalation matrix: who to call at 0/15/30/60 minutes
- Rollforward/rollback instructions (if applicable)
- Post-incident checklist: evidence to collect, owners for RCA actions, timeline capture notes
- Test plan: how to safely exercise this runbook in game days

Example diagnostics snippets

- Check runtime pod health:
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
- Inspect logs for OOMKill or liveness probes:
  kubectl -n redwood logs [pod] --since=10m | grep -E "OOMKilled|liveness probe failed"
- Check queue depth (Redis):
  redis-cli -h redis-svc info | grep "instantaneous_ops_per_sec"

Incident ownership ladder

- T0 (First 10 minutes): Pager recipient acknowledges and triages. If obvious containment step exists, operator executes it.
- T10 (10–30 minutes): Incident Commander (IC) appointed by on-call rotation. IC declares impact and channels (bridge + Slack channel) and assigns roles: comms, triage lead, and mitigation lead.
- T30 (30–90 minutes): Service owner / engineering lead joins. IC maintains timeline and coordinates cross-team dependencies.
- T90+: If unresolved, escalate to SRE manager and Platform Eng lead; consider customer notifications and credits policy.

SLO & severity mapping examples (illustrative)

- P99 latency SLO: <= 150 ms for request-path /v1/generate (global).
- Error rate SLO: 0.02 (2%) errors per 1m window.
- Severity mapping:
  - Sev1 / P1: Revenue-impacting, >50% customers affected, SLO broken for >10 minutes.
  - Sev2 / P2: Significant degradation for subset of customers, SLO degraded but not fully broken.
  - Sev3 / P3: Minor customer impact, isolated errors or performance blips.

On-call rotation stewardship

- Rotation length: 1 week. Primary on-call with a secondary backup.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in PagerDuty notes & Slack):
  1) Current ongoing incidents and bridge links
  2) Outstanding action items requiring follow-up
  3) Recent runbook changes or flaky alerts
  4) Contactable escalations and out-of-hours numbers
- Fairness rules: no more than 2 weekend rotations per quarter; swaps must be logged and approved by the manager.
- Shadowing: new on-call engineers must shadow 2 rotations and complete the on-call checklist exercise in a game day within first 30 days.

Game day (exercise) playbook

Purpose: validate runbooks, surface gaps in escalations, exercise comms and status page flows.

Planning timeline:
- T-21 days: propose scenario and get approval from relevant service owner and SRE lead.
- T-7 days: announce to org with scope and blackout windows.
- T-0: execute exercise in staging or canary region.
- T+1 day: publish game day findings and action items.

Sample game day scenario (KV cache eviction storm):
- Objective: ensure runbook steps contain safe containment for high-throughput prefix-cache misses.
- Roles: IC (SRE on call), operator (service on call), comms (product liaison), observer (engineering steward).
- Exercises:
  1) Trigger synthetic traffic to simulate cache thundering (lower QPS to safe window first).
  2) Follow runbook: rollback deploy, throttle traffic, enable fallback model variant.
  3) Evaluate status page message dissemination and internal bridging.

Postmortem and RCA standard

- When to write: all P1 incidents and either a P2 with customer impact or any incident that required multi-team coordination.
- Template (must be filled):
  - Title: incident-service-date-impact
  - Summary: 2–4 sentence summary
  - Impact: timeline of customer-facing symptoms, number of affected customers, duration
  - Root cause analysis: facts, timeline, gap analysis (tools, people, process)
  - Remediation actions: owner, ETA, verification steps
  - Preventative actions: what will change in monitoring, runbook, or code
  - Postmortem severity and lessons learned
  - Signal evidence: links to logs, graph snapshots, and saved traces
- Postmortem review: present to incident review board within 5 business days. Action items must have owners & due dates.

Status page and customer comms templates

- Principles: be timely, concise, factual, and avoid speculation. Provide regular cadence updates (every 30–60 minutes for P1 until mitigation).

Template: Major Outage (P1)
- Title: [Major Outage] Service name — Degraded / Unavailable
- Initial post (15 min): We are investigating reports of degraded performance for the /v1/generate endpoint. Impact: some customers may see increased latency or errors. We are actively investigating and have started mitigation actions. Next update: in 30 minutes.
- Follow-up post (30 min): Root cause update or actions taken (e.g., "We identified a KV cache thundering event caused by recent rollout X; rolling back to previous model variant and throttling upstream traffic.")
- Restore post: Confirm restoration, provide ETA for full verification, and link to postmortem when available.

Template: Degraded Performance (P2)
- Title: [Degraded Performance] Service name — Elevated error rate
- Initial post: We are seeing an elevated error rate on request-path X affecting a subset of customers. Engineers are investigating. If you are experiencing issues, please contact support with request ID. Next update: 60 minutes.

Customer-facing email snippet (for enterprise customers)

Subject: Incident update — [Service] — {Short description}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We are writing to update you about an incident affecting {Service}. Impact: {brief impact summary}. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue and we anticipate a resolution within {ETA}. We will provide another update at {time}.

If you have urgent concerns, reply to this email or contact your account team.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support (on-call team)

Operational metrics & evidence collection

- Minimum evidence to collect during incident: start/end time, commands run and outputs, screenshots of monitoring graphs, key log snippets, and affected customer IDs. Save snapshots to incident bundle in S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/{incident-id}/.
- Retention: incident bundles retained for 24 months. Postmortems and runbook changes must reference bundle paths.

Runbook testing and acceptance criteria

- Acceptance test: each runbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.
- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.

Escalation and credits policy (brief)

- If an incident leads to an SLA breach (as defined by our contracts), the SRE manager will coordinate with finance and legal on credits. Escalation to account team occurs within 60 minutes for enterprise customers.

Appendix: quick-check triage checklist

1) Acknowledge page and create incident channel.
2) Determine scope: internal-only, subset of customers, or platform-wide.
3) Check SLO dashboards for P99 and error rate.
4) Run core diagnostics (see runbook).
5) If containment exists, execute and mark time.
6) Publish status page initial message and email/Slack to account team.

Appendix: contact matrix (example)

- PagerDuty escalation: On-call primary -> backup -> SRE manager -> Eng Director
- Slack: #inc-ops (bridge), @oncall-team (escalation mentions)

Appendix: sample runbook header (copy into top of each runbook)

Title: runtime-prefix-eviction-P1
Service: redwood-runtime
Steward: Aisha Patel (or assigned engineer)
Created: 2024-11-12
Last reviewed: 2025-02-12
Changelog:
- 2025-02-12: clarified eviction thresholds and added redis diagnostics

Feedback and continued improvement

- If you identify gaps in this policy or the runbook template, open a docs PR and tag @Runbook-Curation. We will incorporate changes monthly and publish a changelog.

Related resources

- SLO dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/slo
- Incident bundle S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/
- Runbook repo: https://git.internal.redwood/runbooks

Approved by: SRE Lead (Diego Morales), Platform Eng Lead (Priya Singh)

Subject: Incident update — [Service] — {Short description}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We are writing to update you about an incident affecting {Service}. Impact: {brief impact summary}. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue and we anticipate a resolution within {ETA}. We will provide another update at {time}.

If you have urgent concerns, reply to this email or contact your account team.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support (on-call team)

Operational metrics & evidence collection

- Minimum evidence to collect during incident: start/end time, commands run and outputs, screenshots of monitoring graphs, key log snippets, and affected customer IDs. Save snapshots to incident bundle in S3: s3://redwood-incident-bundles/{incident-id}/.
- Retention: incident bundles retained for 24 months. Postmortems and runbook changes must reference bundle paths.

Runbook testing and acceptance criteria

- Acceptance test: each runbook must have at least one automated smoke test (synthetic check) run monthly. Tests should validate that diagnostics produce expected outputs and that containment steps are safe in staging.
- Test results should be attached to runbook metadata with last-test date and test-run author.

Appendix: quick-check triage checklist

1) Acknowledge page and create incident channel.
2) Determine scope: internal-only, subset of customers, or platform-wide.
3) Check SLO dashboards for P99 and error rate.
4) Run core diagnostics (see runbook).
5) If containment exists, execute and mark time.
6) Publish status page initial message and email/Slack to account team.

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-release-engineering\n\n1-release-train-slot-for-rollout-plan-migration\n\nContent: Doc owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)\nLast reviewed with: Platform Control Plane (Ethan), Routing (Mina), Telemetry (Logan), SRE (Rafael), Console (Chloe), Security (Kaitlyn)\n\nPurpose\n- Single checklist for GA launch of Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools: flags, DB migrations/backfills, canary + enablement plan, monitoring, comms, and rollback.\n- This is the “release train” view; detailed operational steps are in the Confluence runbook.\n\nDefinitions / components in scope\n- Control plane: DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan model + APIs (create/update/promote/abort/hold/force-promote)\n- Policy engine: gate evaluation v1 (latency/error/saturation + missing-data semantics)\n- Routing/data plane: stage-based partition selection for Dedicated pools (multi-region aware)\n- Telemetry: stage tags in metrics/traces + dashboards/alerts\n- Console: timeline view + gate evidence retrieval + action availability (promote/abort/hold)\n- Security/compliance: audit events for rollout actions + export/SIEM pipeline\n\nFeature flags (authoritative list for GA)\n- Flag naming here matches config repo conventions; confirm exact keys in prod config before go/no-go.\n\n[ ] FF1: dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled\n    - Master kill switch for all staged rollouts on Dedicated pools.\n    - Expected default: OFF globally; ON for internal pools + allowlisted customer accounts/pools.\n\n[ ] FF2: dedicated_staged_rollouts.control_plane_api\n    - Enables create/update/get/list for rollout plans + promotion/abort/hold endpoints.\n    - Expected default: ON in staging; ON in prod (guarded by authz and allowlist).\n\n[ ] FF3: dedicated_staged_rollouts.routing_stage_partitioning\n    - Enables stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection in routing.\n    - Expected default: OFF in prod until canary.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-release-engineering\n\nendpoints.\n    - Expected default: ON in staging; ON in prod (guarded by authz and allowlist).\n\n[ ] FF3: dedicated_staged_rollouts.routing_stage_partitioning\n    - Enables stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection in routing.\n    - Expected default: OFF in prod until canary.\n\n[ ] FF4: dedicated_staged_rollouts.gate_eval_v1\n    - Enables automated gate evaluation in policy engine.\n    - Missing metrics behavior: FAIL-CLOSED (i.e., “Unknown” -> block promotion) with manual override available to admins.\n\n[ ] FF5: dedicated_staged_rollouts.emit_stage_tags\n    - Adds stage_id/stage_name (or equivalent) tags/labels to key metrics/traces.\n    - Must be paired with cardinality limits (allowlist) and sampling settings from telemetry team.\n\n[ ] FF6: dedicated_staged_rollouts.console_timeline\n    - Enables Console UI workflow elements + backend endpoints for stage timeline and evidence.\n\n[ ] FF7: dedicated_staged_rollouts.force_override_admin\n    - Enables force-promote and hold controls; gated by admin role.\n    - Must write explicit audit events with “override=true” + reason.\n\nDB migrations / schema readiness\n[ ] M1: Apply rollout plan schema migration (PR-28411)\n    - Tables/columns expected:\n      - dedicated_pool_rollout_plans (or equivalent)\n      - stage definitions (json/blob) with stable stage IDs\n      - rollout state machine fields: draft/running/held/aborted/completed\n      - optimistic concurrency (etag/version) + idempotency key storage for promote/abort\n\n[ ] M2: Validate forward/backward compatibility\n    - Old routing path works when routing_stage_partitioning is OFF.\n    - Control plane reads/writes safe under mixed-version service deployment.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-release-engineering\n\nC2.2: Enable routing_stage_partitioning for those pools.\n[ ] C2.3: Enable emit_stage_tags for those pools (watch cardinality).\n[ ] C2.4: Run controlled staged rollout of a harmless change (e.g., routing policy toggle) and verify promotion annotations + gate evaluation.\n\nPhase 3 — Limited external beta (design partners)\n[ ] C3.1: Confirm allowlisted accounts/pools (tracked via INT-1933).\n[ ] C3.2: Enable per account/pool (avoid partial region exposure unless explicitly desired).\n[ ] C3.3: Provide customer comms: expectations, how to interpret holds/aborts, escalation path.\n[ ] C3.4: Monitor for known failure mode: canary partition starving capacity and causing 429 spikes (SUP-28522 learnings).\n\nPhase 4 — GA enablement\n[ ] C4.1: Default availability: staged rollouts feature available to all Dedicated accounts (or tiered rollout by customer segment per Product).\n[ ] C4.2: Confirm support readiness: macros, oncall routing, escalation policy.\n\nCustomer + internal comms plan\n[ ] COM1: Release notes drafted (internal + customer-facing)\n    - Include: what staged rollouts are, default stage templates, what gates are evaluated, what “hold/abort” means.\n\n[ ] COM2: Internal enablement\n    - #eng-oncall playbook update + short training\n    - TAM/CS brief (what customers will see in Console; how to request enablement)\n\n[ ] COM3: Customer announcement\n    - Target segment: Dedicated admins/operators\n    - Include: how to request enablement (if allowlist), docs link, limitations (no arbitrary custom metrics in v1)\n\n[ ] COM4: Change management packet for regulated customers (if needed)\n    - Audit event coverage summary\n    - Retention/export statement\n    - RBAC overview",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-release-engineering\n\n/operators\n    - Include: how to request enablement (if allowlist), docs link, limitations (no arbitrary custom metrics in v1)\n\n[ ] COM4: Change management packet for regulated customers (if needed)\n    - Audit event coverage summary\n    - Retention/export statement\n    - RBAC overview\n\nRollback plan (must be executable in <15 minutes)\nPrinciples\n- Prefer flag rollback over code rollback.\n- Rollback should revert routing behavior first (protect SLOs), then disable promotion actions, then reduce telemetry surface.\n\nRollback triggers (examples)\n- Elevated 429s or sustained queue depth spike in canary stage indicating capacity starvation.\n- Routing misassignment across stage partitions or region bleed.\n- Gate evaluation instability causing repeated false aborts/holds.\n- Telemetry cardinality incident.\n\nRollback steps (ordered)\n[ ] R1: Disable routing_stage_partitioning in prod for affected pools/accounts (or globally if unclear scope).\n    - Expected effect: all traffic routes to stable partition/path; staged rollout becomes no-op.\n\n[ ] R2: Disable gate_eval_v1 (if gate system suspected)\n    - Expected effect: promotion blocks or reverts to manual-only behavior depending on implementation; confirm with Platform.\n\n[ ] R3: Disable console_timeline (if Console endpoints failing / confusing)\n    - Expected effect: hide staged rollout workflow; prevent customer actions.\n\n[ ] R4: Disable emit_stage_tags (if telemetry cardinality issues)\n    - Note: dashboards will lose stage breakdown; keep baseline pool dashboards.\n\n[ ] R5: Disable master flag dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled\n\n[ ] R6: If DB migration issue suspected\n    - DO NOT attempt down-migration during incident.\n    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.\n\n[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation\n    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).\n    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Launch checklist — Dedicated staged rollouts (reserved pools) — GA\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-release-engineering\n\ndown-migration during incident.\n    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.\n\n[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation\n    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).\n    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.\n\nOpen items / final sign-offs (must be checked before GA)\n[ ] S1: SRE (Rafael/Sean): alert routing + runbook sign-off.\n[ ] S2: Security (Kaitlyn): RBAC + audit log completeness sign-off.\n[ ] S3: Telemetry (Logan/Allison): cardinality controls + dashboard templates sign-off.\n[ ] S4: Routing (Mina): multi-region impairment behavior sign-off.\n[ ] S5: Console (Chloe/Jada): customer-facing UX copy + evidence rendering sign-off.\n[ ] S6: Release Eng (Connor): release train slot confirmed + staged rollout of flags scheduled.\n\nNotes / lessons learned to carry forward\n- Capacity fragmentation risk is highest for small Dedicated pools; ensure validation rules block stages that would create under-sized partitions.\n- Missing metrics must not silently pass gates; fail-closed with explicit override + audit is the accepted v1 stance.\n- Canary stage can create unexpected effective capacity reduction; watch for 429 spikes and queue depth growth within first 10 minutes of canary enablement.\n\nTitle Field Name: title\n\n## Content Field Names\n\n- content\n\nDataset Doc Uuid: dsid_62bd575d44e5409abddcf9836f6f8f6a",

  "content": "Doc owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last reviewed with: Platform Control Plane (Ethan), Routing (Mina), Telemetry (Logan), SRE (Rafael), Console (Chloe), Security (Kaitlyn)

Purpose
- Single checklist for GA launch of Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools: flags, DB migrations/backfills, canary + enablement plan, monitoring, comms, and rollback.
- This is the “release train” view; detailed operational steps are in the Confluence runbook.

Definitions / components in scope
- Control plane: DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan model + APIs (create/update/promote/abort/hold/force-promote)
- Policy engine: gate evaluation v1 (latency/error/saturation + missing-data semantics)
- Routing/data plane: stage-based partition selection for Dedicated pools (multi-region aware)
- Telemetry: stage tags in metrics/traces + dashboards/alerts
- Console: timeline view + gate evidence retrieval + action availability (promote/abort/hold)
- Security/compliance: audit events for rollout actions + export/SIEM pipeline

Feature flags (authoritative list for GA)
- Flag naming here matches config repo conventions; confirm exact keys in prod config before go/no-go.

[ ] FF1: dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled
    - Master kill switch for all staged rollouts on Dedicated pools.
    - Expected default: OFF globally; ON for internal pools + allowlisted customer accounts/pools.

[ ] FF2: dedicated_staged_rollouts.control_plane_api
    - Enables create/update/get/list for rollout plans + promotion/abort/hold endpoints.
    - Expected default: ON in staging; ON in prod (guarded by authz and allowlist).

[ ] FF3: dedicated_staged_rollouts.routing_stage_partitioning
    - Enables stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection in routing.
    - Expected default: OFF in prod until canary.

[ ] FF4: dedicated_staged_rollouts.gate_eval_v1
    - Enables automated gate evaluation in policy engine.
    - Missing metrics behavior: FAIL-CLOSED (i.e., “Unknown” -> block promotion) with manual override available to admins.

[ ] FF5: dedicated_staged_rollouts.emit_stage_tags
    - Adds stage_id/stage_name (or equivalent) tags/labels to key metrics/traces.
    - Must be paired with cardinality limits (allowlist) and sampling settings from telemetry team.

[ ] FF6: dedicated_staged_rollouts.console_timeline
    - Enables Console UI workflow elements + backend endpoints for stage timeline and evidence.

[ ] FF7: dedicated_staged_rollouts.force_override_admin
    - Enables force-promote and hold controls; gated by admin role.
    - Must write explicit audit events with “override=true” + reason.


DB migrations / schema readiness
[ ] M1: Apply rollout plan schema migration (PR-28411)
    - Tables/columns expected:
      - dedicated_pool_rollout_plans (or equivalent)
      - stage definitions (json/blob) with stable stage IDs
      - rollout state machine fields: draft/running/held/aborted/completed
      - optimistic concurrency (etag/version) + idempotency key storage for promote/abort

[ ] M2: Validate forward/backward compatibility
    - Old routing path works when routing_stage_partitioning is OFF.
    - Control plane reads/writes safe under mixed-version service deployment.

[ ] M3: Backfill plan (if required)
    - Decision: DO NOT auto-create rollout plans for all existing Dedicated pools at GA; only create when customer/operator initiates OR when allowlisted account is enabled.
    - If there is any required backfill (e.g., default empty plan rows for allowlisted pools), confirm batch job:
      - Rate limiting (avoid DB hotspots)
      - Idempotent reruns
      - Metrics: rows inserted/updated, failures, duration

[ ] M4: Data retention / cleanup
    - Confirm retention for plan history + audit events aligns with Dedicated/enterprise expectations.
    - Confirm any TTL jobs won’t delete active plan state.


Audit logging & compliance readiness
[ ] A1: Audit events emitted for actions
    - create_plan, update_plan, start_rollout (if separate), promote_stage, abort_rollout, hold_rollout, resume_rollout, force_promote, force_abort (if supported)
    - Required fields: actor, actor_type, account_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, previous_stage, new_stage, override_flag, reason, idempotency_key, request_id, timestamp.

[ ] A2: Audit export pipeline includes new event types (Jira INT-1951)
    - Verify export mapping, indexing, and filtering.
    - Verify enterprise export targets (SIEM) receive events within SLA.

[ ] A3: RBAC verified (Kaitlyn sign-off)
    - Customer admin vs Redwood operator vs Redwood admin distinctions documented.
    - Force-promote requires elevated permission; Console UI must surface warning + require reason.


Telemetry, dashboards, alerting
[ ] T1: Stage-tagged metrics/traces enabled behind emit_stage_tags
    - Verify cardinality guardrails:
      - allowlisted labels only
      - stage_id is stable and bounded (no per-request randomness)
      - sampling applied to traces as needed
    - Confirm hotfix PR-28644 (cardinality regression) is included in release.

[ ] T2: Dashboards deployed (observability-pack PR-631)
    - Required panels:
      - error rate (4xx/5xx) by stage + region
      - p95/p99 latency by stage + region
      - saturation/headroom (GPU util / queue depth)
      - OOM rate / GPU health indicators
      - 429/request drop signals by stage
      - annotations for promotions/aborts/holds

[ ] T3: Alerts configured + routed
    - Gate failure alerts: ticket vs page thresholds agreed with SRE.
    - Ownership:
      - routing partitioning failures -> Routing oncall
      - gate eval pipeline issues -> Policy/Telemetry oncall
      - control plane API errors -> Platform oncall
    - Verify alert noise controls (minimum sample size / windowing).


Performance / reliability gates for GA (go/no-go criteria)
[ ] G1: Integration tests green in CI (PR-28610)
    - Must cover: create plan → start → promote → gate fail → abort/rollback; missing metrics; idempotent promote; concurrent promote requests.

[ ] G2: Canary simulation / load test results archived
    - Demonstrate no regression in:
      - baseline latency at 100% stable stage
      - error rate at stable stage with feature flags OFF
      - routing correctness under multi-region impairment scenario

[ ] G3: SRE sign-off
    - Runbook reviewed and oncall steps are clear.
    - “No promote during incident/high error budget burn” policy documented (even if enforced manually initially).

[ ] G4: Console readiness
    - Gate evidence renders correctly and matches backend queries.
    - Action availability correct (promote blocked when gates fail/unknown, unless override permission).


Canary / rollout plan for production enablement
Phase 0 — Staging verification
[ ] C0.1: Deploy to staging with all flags ON.
[ ] C0.2: Create test Dedicated pool + test plan with default stages: 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% (or replica partitions where applicable).
[ ] C0.3: Validate:
    - promote path
    - abort path
    - hold/resume path
    - missing-metrics behavior shows “Unknown” and blocks promote

Phase 1 — Prod dark launch (no functional change)
[ ] C1.1: Deploy prod services with routing_stage_partitioning OFF.
[ ] C1.2: Enable control_plane_api ON (still safe if no one uses it; RBAC enforced).
[ ] C1.3: Validate API health + DB metrics (connections, query latency).

Phase 2 — Internal canary
[ ] C2.1: Enable dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled for internal Redwood Dedicated pools only.
[ ] C2.2: Enable routing_stage_partitioning for those pools.
[ ] C2.3: Enable emit_stage_tags for those pools (watch cardinality).
[ ] C2.4: Run controlled staged rollout of a harmless change (e.g., routing policy toggle) and verify promotion annotations + gate evaluation.

Phase 3 — Limited external beta (design partners)
[ ] C3.1: Confirm allowlisted accounts/pools (tracked via INT-1933).
[ ] C3.2: Enable per account/pool (avoid partial region exposure unless explicitly desired).
[ ] C3.3: Provide customer comms: expectations, how to interpret holds/aborts, escalation path.
[ ] C3.4: Monitor for known failure mode: canary partition starving capacity and causing 429 spikes (SUP-28522 learnings).

Phase 4 — GA enablement
[ ] C4.1: Default availability: staged rollouts feature available to all Dedicated accounts (or tiered rollout by customer segment per Product).
[ ] C4.2: Confirm support readiness: macros, oncall routing, escalation policy.


Customer + internal comms plan
[ ] COM1: Release notes drafted (internal + customer-facing)
    - Include: what staged rollouts are, default stage templates, what gates are evaluated, what “hold/abort” means.

[ ] COM2: Internal enablement
    - #eng-oncall playbook update + short training
    - TAM/CS brief (what customers will see in Console; how to request enablement)

[ ] COM3: Customer announcement
    - Target segment: Dedicated admins/operators
    - Include: how to request enablement (if allowlist), docs link, limitations (no arbitrary custom metrics in v1)

[ ] COM4: Change management packet for regulated customers (if needed)
    - Audit event coverage summary
    - Retention/export statement
    - RBAC overview


Rollback plan (must be executable in <15 minutes)
Principles
- Prefer flag rollback over code rollback.
- Rollback should revert routing behavior first (protect SLOs), then disable promotion actions, then reduce telemetry surface.

Rollback triggers (examples)
- Elevated 429s or sustained queue depth spike in canary stage indicating capacity starvation.
- Routing misassignment across stage partitions or region bleed.
- Gate evaluation instability causing repeated false aborts/holds.
- Telemetry cardinality incident.

Rollback steps (ordered)
[ ] R1: Disable routing_stage_partitioning in prod for affected pools/accounts (or globally if unclear scope).
    - Expected effect: all traffic routes to stable partition/path; staged rollout becomes no-op.

[ ] R2: Disable gate_eval_v1 (if gate system suspected)
    - Expected effect: promotion blocks or reverts to manual-only behavior depending on implementation; confirm with Platform.

[ ] R3: Disable console_timeline (if Console endpoints failing / confusing)
    - Expected effect: hide staged rollout workflow; prevent customer actions.

[ ] R4: Disable emit_stage_tags (if telemetry cardinality issues)
    - Note: dashboards will lose stage breakdown; keep baseline pool dashboards.

[ ] R5: Disable master flag dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled

[ ] R6: If DB migration issue suspected
    - DO NOT attempt down-migration during incident.
    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.

[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation
    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).
    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.


Open items / final sign-offs (must be checked before GA)
[ ] S1: SRE (Rafael/Sean): alert routing + runbook sign-off.
[ ] S2: Security (Kaitlyn): RBAC + audit log completeness sign-off.
[ ] S3: Telemetry (Logan/Allison): cardinality controls + dashboard templates sign-off.
[ ] S4: Routing (Mina): multi-region impairment behavior sign-off.
[ ] S5: Console (Chloe/Jada): customer-facing UX copy + evidence rendering sign-off.
[ ] S6: Release Eng (Connor): release train slot confirmed + staged rollout of flags scheduled.

Notes / lessons learned to carry forward
- Capacity fragmentation risk is highest for small Dedicated pools; ensure validation rules block stages that would create under-sized partitions.
- Missing metrics must not silently pass gates; fail-closed with explicit override + audit is the accepted v1 stance.
- Canary stage can create unexpected effective capacity reduction; watch for 429 spikes and queue depth growth within first 10 minutes of canary enablement.

Rollback plan (must be executable in <15 minutes)
Principles
- Prefer flag rollback over code rollback.
- Rollback should revert routing behavior first (protect SLOs), then disable promotion actions, then reduce telemetry surface.

Rollback triggers (examples)
- Elevated 429s or sustained queue depth spike in canary stage indicating capacity starvation.
- Routing misassignment across stage partitions or region bleed.
- Gate evaluation instability causing repeated false aborts/holds.
- Telemetry cardinality incident.

Rollback steps (ordered)
[ ] R1: Disable routing_stage_partitioning in prod for affected pools/accounts (or globally if unclear scope).
    - Expected effect: all traffic routes to stable partition/path; staged rollout becomes no-op.

[ ] R2: Disable gate_eval_v1 (if gate system suspected)
    - Expected effect: promotion blocks or reverts to manual-only behavior depending on implementation; confirm with Platform.

[ ] R3: Disable console_timeline (if Console endpoints failing / confusing)
    - Expected effect: hide staged rollout workflow; prevent customer actions.

[ ] R4: Disable emit_stage_tags (if telemetry cardinality issues)
    - Note: dashboards will lose stage breakdown; keep baseline pool dashboards.

[ ] R5: Disable master flag dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled

[ ] R6: If DB migration issue suspected
    - DO NOT attempt down-migration during incident.
    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.

[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation
    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).
    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.

  "content": "## Overview\nThis program formalizes Redwood Inference\u2019s tiered reliability commitments by defining canonical SLIs/SLOs for **Hosted (shared)** vs **Dedicated (reserved capacity)**, and adopting a consistent, enforced **error budget policy** that connects reliability outcomes to operational behavior (alerting, incident triggers, and release controls).\n\nThis page is the Q1 2026 program overview (motivation, scope, milestones, owners, dependencies, and success metrics). Detailed definitions and policy are maintained in the linked pages under **SLOs & Error Budgets**.\n\n---\n\n## Why we are doing this (motivation)\nCustomer escalations in late 2025 and early 2026 highlighted recurring gaps:\n- **Latency spikes during burst traffic** (especially p95/p99) causing customer-visible degradation and unpredictable throughput.\n- Elevated **5xx rates** and **stream disconnects** during rollouts and/or capacity pressure.\n- Mismatch between **Product SLA language** and **Engineering measurement/enforcement** (what \u201ccounts,\u201d where we measure, and what we do when we are burning budget).\n\nWe will standardize measurement and align operational actions to reliability outcomes so that:\n- Engineering can evaluate changes against objective SLO targets.\n- SRE/Infra can respond consistently using budget burn-rate signals.\n- Product/CS/SE can set correct expectations and communicate tier-specific impact.\n\n---\n\n## Program goals (Q1 2026)\n1) **Define canonical SLIs and tier-specific SLO targets** for key request paths across regions.\n2) **Adopt an error budget policy** with burn-rate alerting, clear breach definitions, and an escalation/mitigation ladder.\n3) **Implement enforcement** via dashboards, alert rules, and phased CI/deploy gates.\n4) **Codify graceful degradation expectations per tier** (routing/fallback/overload shedding) and how those behaviors impact SLI accounting.\n5) **Roll out to stakeholders** and create customer-facing alignment artifacts (SLO\u2192SLA mapping, tier-specific escalation expectations).\n\n---\n\n## In scope\n### Tiers\n- **Hosted (shared)**: multi-tenant platform, tiered by product plan but measured at the platform tier level for this phase.\n- **Dedicated (reserved capacity)**: per-account pools (or logically isolated capacity), stricter and more predictable reliability commitments.\n\n> Note: **Private** (VPC/on-prem) is referenced for future work, but not included in enforcement or gating in this phase.\n\n### Services / request path boundaries\n- API gateway\n- Routing / control plane policy evaluation\n- Model serving request path\n- Observability pipelines required to compute SLIs (metrics + events)\n\n### Primary SLIs\n- **Request success rate** (non-5xx)\n- **End-to-end latency percentiles** (p50 / p95 / p99)\n- **Streaming reliability** (disconnect/error events)\n\n### Exclusions (high-level)\nExclusions are standardized in the SLI spec and SLO definitions pages, but at a minimum this program explicitly addresses:\n- Filtering invalid requests (4xx validation) and rate-limited requests (429) from \u201cservice reliability\u201d accounting.\n- Rules for client aborts vs server disconnects for streaming.\n- Retry and fallback accounting rules (to avoid double-counting while preserving user-perceived reliability).\n\n---\n\n## Out of scope (Q1 2026)\n- Contract changes for Private / on-prem.\n- Per-model SLO commitments (we will expose \u201ctop contributors\u201d without committing to per-model SLOs).\n- Unlimited cardinality breakouts (per-customer/per-model/per-route everywhere). Where needed, we will add controlled breakdowns with strict guardrails.\n\n---\n\n## Guiding principles\n- **One set of canonical definitions.** There must be a single source of truth for \u201csuccess,\u201d \u201clatency,\u201d and \u201cstreaming failure.\u201d\n- **Tier tags at ingest, preserved through routing.** Tier labeling must be correct at ingress and propagated across retries/fallback.\n- **Budgets drive behavior.** Error budgets are not passive reporting; they gate risk (with phased enforcement).\n- **Graceful degradation is a feature, not an accident.** Fallback and overload shedding must be intentional and consistently accounted for.\n- **Gradual enforcement.** Warn-only \u2192 soft gates \u2192 hard gates, with an emergency fix path.\n\n---\n\n## Deliverables\n### Documentation (Confluence)\n- Tiered SLO definitions and SLI formulas (Hosted vs Dedicated)\n- Error budget policy and enforcement rules\n- Observability SLI specification for gateway/routing\n- Runbooks and incident process updates\n\n### Engineering assets\n- Tier-aware SLI metrics and event taxonomy\n- SLO config schema + validation tooling\n- Error budget computation pipeline (rolling windows) + data quality checks\n- Dashboards + burn-rate alerts\n- CI/CD deploy gates (warn-only then enforced)\n\n### Customer-facing alignment artifacts\n- SLO \u2192 SLA mapping and exclusion alignment\n- Tier-specific escalation expectations for CS/SE\n- (Dedicated) customer SLO reporting view and access model\n\n---\n\n## Milestones and timeline (Q1 2026)\nThis is a quarter-scale rollout. Dates are targets; execution uses Linear tickets referenced from the program board.\n\n### Phase 1 \u2014 Discovery + SLI definitions (2\u20133 weeks)\n**Outcome:** Agreement on measurement boundaries and canonical event/metric definitions.\n- Finalize SLIs: success/error semantics, latency measurement points, streaming rules, exclusions.\n- Validate tier labeling approach and propagation rules.\n- Identify data quality gaps (missing tags, inconsistent status codes, incomplete streaming events).\n\n### Phase 2 \u2014 SLO target proposal + review (2 weeks)\n**Outcome:** Signed-off tier-specific SLO targets per endpoint class and region.\n- Produce target matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated by endpoint (chat/completions, embeddings, streaming).\n- Review feasibility with Infra (capacity headroom) and Routing (fallback behavior).\n- Product approval and documentation of rationale and trade-offs.\n\n### Phase 3 \u2014 Implementation (3\u20135 weeks)\n**Outcome:** Dashboards, alerting, and budget computation live; initial policy hooks in CI.\n- Dashboards: per-tier and regional views, \u201ctop contributors,\u201d links to traces/logs.\n- Multi-window burn-rate alerts + paging policy (severity mapping).\n- Budget calculation job (rolling windows), backfill approach, and data quality checks.\n- Deploy gate (warn-only) tied to budget burn state.\n\n### Phase 4 \u2014 Rollout + training (2 weeks)\n**Outcome:** Operationalized program across on-call, CS/SE, and Product.\n- On-call playbooks and mitigation runbook updates.\n- CS escalation playbook updated, including intake template and expectations by tier.\n- Dedicated customer comms plan and enablement.\n- Move from warn-only to enforced gating for non-critical deploys (with emergency override path).\n\n---\n\n## Ownership and RACI\n### Core owners\n- **Executive sponsors:** Ava Chen (CTO), Priya Natarajan (VP Eng Platform), Neha Kapoor (VP Infra & Reliability)\n- **Program sponsor:** Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE)\n- **Program manager:** Talia Benson\n- **Delivery lead:** Rafael Mendes (SRE Mgr)\n- **SLO/error budget implementation lead:** Aisha Bello (Senior SRE)\n\n### Key workstream owners\n- **SLI instrumentation (gateway):** Amara Diallo\n- **Tier tagging / propagation:** Mina Haddad (Routing), Ravi Menon (Architecture), Elena Popov (Implementation)\n- **Telemetry platform:** Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson (ingestion), Thomas Baird (cardinality controls)\n- **Dashboards/alerts:** Sergio Costa\n- **Deploy gates:** Jordan Lee, Connor O'Brien, Sahana Iyer\n- **Product alignment:** Nikhil Sharma (Hosted), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Evelyn Hart (sponsor)\n- **Customer-facing enablement:** Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim, Markus Klein, Elliot Price\n\n### RACI (summary)\n| Decision / Deliverable | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Canonical SLI definitions + exclusions | Aisha Bello | Sean Gallagher | Mina Haddad, Logan Wright, Nikhil Sharma, Lauren Bishop | Eng org |\n| Tiered SLO targets | Rafael Mendes | Evelyn Hart | Neha Kapoor, Mina Haddad, Nikhil/Lauren | CS/SE |\n| Error budget policy | Aisha Bello | Sean Gallagher | Priya Natarajan, Neha Kapoor | Eng + Product |\n| Dashboards + burn-rate alerts | Sergio Costa | Rafael Mendes | Logan Wright, Thomas Baird | On-call rotations |\n| Deploy gate phasing | Jordan Lee | Priya Natarajan | Connor O'Brien, Sahana Iyer, SRE | Eng + Product |\n| SLO\u2192SLA mapping | Elliot Price | Evelyn Hart | Legal (as needed), CS, SRE | Sales/CS |\n\n---\n\n## Dependencies\n### Technical dependencies\n- **Tier-aware tagging at ingress** must be implemented and validated end-to-end (gateway \u2192 routing \u2192 serving \u2192 telemetry).\n- **Event taxonomy for streaming** must distinguish: client abort vs server disconnect vs upstream timeout.\n- **Recording rules and aggregation strategy** must avoid cardinality explosion while preserving actionable breakdowns (tier, endpoint class, region; limited \u201ctop-N\u201d model/route views).\n- **SLO config schema** must support tier/region/endpoint scoping and be validated in CI.\n\n### Process dependencies\n- Agreement with Product on:\n  - Which SLOs are internal-only vs shareable for Dedicated reporting.\n  - Which exclusions are appropriate for customer-facing SLAs.\n- Updated incident process tying burn-rate to incident classification and comms requirements.\n\n---\n\n## Enforcement model (phased)\nThis program intentionally stages enforcement to avoid blocking critical reliability fixes early on.\n\n1) **Visibility first** (dashboards + annotations)\n- SLO dashboards available for Hosted and Dedicated.\n- Deploy and incident annotations visible on SLO timelines.\n\n2) **Alerting** (multi-window burn-rate)\n- Burn-rate alerts page correct rotations.\n- Alerts link directly to dashboards, traces, and mitigation runbooks.\n\n3) **Warn-only gates**\n- CI/CD checks evaluate current error budget state.\n- Gate posts warnings (Slack + deploy output) and logs any overrides.\n\n4) **Enforced gates**\n- When a tier is in a red state (budget exhausted or acute burn), block non-emergency deploys.\n- Emergency fixes permitted via explicit override procedure with audit trail.\n\n---\n\n## Graceful degradation (expectations by tier)\nWe will document tier-specific behavior and ensure SLI accounting aligns with user impact.\n\n**Hosted (shared):**\n- Prefer platform stability under overload: bounded queues, overload shedding, and controlled fallback to compatible variants.\n- Expect more aggressive protective measures (rate limiting, load shedding) to protect shared infrastructure.\n\n**Dedicated:**\n- Prioritize predictability: capacity headroom commitments, fast mitigation via fleet actions, and conservative fallback policies.\n- Customer-specific dashboards and incident comms should reflect dedicated impact separately from Hosted.\n\n> Important: Fallback/retry behavior must not \u201chide\u201d failures by shifting the user-visible failure mode. Accounting will follow the SLI spec (including how retries are deduplicated and how final user outcome is counted).\n\n---\n\n## Success metrics\n### Reliability outcomes (measurable)\n- Tiered SLO dashboards show stable data coverage (no major metric gaps) across in-scope regions.\n- Burn-rate alerts have an acceptable signal-to-noise ratio (tracked by SRE):\n  - < 15% alerts classified as \u201cactionless / data issue\u201d after tuning period.\n- Reduced recurrence of top customer escalations:\n  - Fewer P0/P1 escalations due to latency spikes and streaming disconnect ambiguity.\n\n### Operational outcomes\n- On-call can execute a consistent playbook for budget burn (traffic shaping, fallback policy adjustments, capacity actions, rollbacks).\n- Release risk is explicitly managed:\n  - When budget is constrained, risky rollouts are deferred or require higher scrutiny.\n\n### Org / alignment outcomes\n- Product SLA language and internal SLO measurement are aligned (documented mapping exists, with clear exclusions).\n- CS/SE have an intake + escalation workflow tied to tiers and dashboards.\n\n---\n\n## Risks and mitigations\n- **Risk: Metric cardinality explosion** (per-model/per-customer labels in hot-path metrics).\n  - Mitigation: strict label allowlist; \u201ctop-N contributors\u201d computed in controlled pipelines; dedicated account dashboards use scoped access and pre-aggregation.\n\n- **Risk: Incorrect tier labeling** leading to invalid SLO reporting.\n  - Mitigation: enforce tagging at ingress; add propagation tests; compare tag coverage in telemetry validation job; block rollout if tag coverage falls below threshold.\n\n- **Risk: Gating blocks critical fixes** early in adoption.\n  - Mitigation: phased enforcement; emergency override path; exceptions reviewed weekly by SRE + Platform.\n\n- **Risk: Fallback masks failures and confuses customers.**\n  - Mitigation: explicit \u201cdegradation modes\u201d documented; SLI accounting rules published; comms templates include tier-specific impact and degradation behavior.\n\n---\n\n## Communication plan\n- Weekly update in **#eng-sre** and **#eng-platform** with milestone status and upcoming changes.\n- Product checkpoint at end of Phase 2 to approve targets and customer-facing messaging.\n- CS/SE enablement session during Phase 4 covering:\n  - How to interpret tier dashboards and budget state\n  - What data to collect for escalations\n  - Expected timelines and comms flow during a budget breach\n\n---\n\n## How to engage / escalation\n- Questions about definitions/exclusions: contact **Aisha Bello** or **Rafael Mendes**.\n- Routing/fallback behavior questions: contact **Mina Haddad**.\n- Deploy gate behavior and overrides: contact **Jordan Lee**.\n- Customer-facing alignment: contact **Elliot Price** (docs) and **Rachel Kim** (enterprise escalation).\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A \u2014 Canonical artifacts (links)\n- Tiered SLO definitions: *Tiered SLO Definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated)*\n- Error budget policy: *Error Budget Policy & Enforcement*\n- SLI spec: *SLI Specification \u2014 API Gateway & Routing*\n- ADR-0142: *Tier-aware SLI Tagging at Ingress*\n- ADR-0143: *Burn-rate Alerting Approach*\n- Dashboards spec: *Tiered SLO Dashboards & Alerts Spec*\n- Mitigation runbook: *Error Budget Breach Mitigation Runbook*\n- Incident process: *Error Budget Breach Incident Process*\n- SLO\u2192SLA mapping: *Tiered SLO to SLA Mapping (Hosted & Dedicated)*\n",

      "text": "[Document context]
Title: Tiered SLOs + Error Budget Program (Q1 2026)
Source: EnterpriseRAG/confluence
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/tiered-slo-and-error-budget-program-q1-2026.json
Connector: confluence
Workspace: eng-sre

izes Redwood Inference’s tiered reliability commitments by defining canonical SLIs/SLOs for **Hosted (shared)** vs **Dedicated (reserved capacity)**, and adopting a consistent, enforced **error budget policy** that connects reliability outcomes to operational behavior (alerting, incident triggers, and release controls).

This page is the Q1 2026 program overview (motivation, scope, milestones, owners, dependencies, and success metrics). Detailed definitions and policy are maintained in the linked pages under **SLOs & Error Budgets**.

---

## Why we are doing this (motivation)
Customer escalations in late 2025 and early 2026 highlighted recurring gaps:
- **Latency spikes during burst traffic** (especially p95/p99) causing customer-visible degradation and unpredictable throughput.
- Elevated **5xx rates** and **stream disconnects** during rollouts and/or capacity pressure.
- Mismatch between **Product SLA language** and **Engineering measurement/enforcement** (what “counts,” where we measure, and what we do when we are burning budget).

We will standardize measurement and align operational actions to reliability outcomes so that:
- Engineering can evaluate changes against objective SLO targets.
- SRE/Infra can respond consistently using budget burn-rate signals.
- Product/CS/SE can set correct expectations and communicate tier-specific impact.

---

## Program goals (Q1 2026)
1) **Define canonical SLIs and tier-specific SLO targets** for key request paths across regions.
2) **Adopt an error budget policy** with burn-rate alerting, clear breach definitions, and an escalation/mitigation ladder.
3) **Implement enforcement** via dashboards, alert rules, and phased CI/deploy gates.
4) **Codify graceful degradation expectations per tier** (routing/fallback/overload shedding) and how those behaviors impact SLI accounting.
5) **Roll out to stakeholders** and create customer-facing alignment artifacts (SLO→SLA mapping, tier-specific escalation expectations).

phased CI/deploy gates.
4) **Codify graceful degradation expectations per tier** (routing/fallback/overload shedding) and how those behaviors impact SLI accounting.
5) **Roll out to stakeholders** and create customer-facing alignment artifacts (SLO→SLA mapping, tier-specific escalation expectations).

---

## In scope
### Tiers
- **Hosted (shared)**: multi-tenant platform, tiered by product plan but measured at the platform tier level for this phase.
- **Dedicated (reserved capacity)**: per-account pools (or logically isolated capacity), stricter and more predictable reliability commitments.

> Note: **Private** (VPC/on-prem) is referenced for future work, but not included in enforcement or gating in this phase.

### Services / request path boundaries
- API gateway
- Routing / control plane policy evaluation
- Model serving request path
- Observability pipelines required to compute SLIs (metrics + events)

### Primary SLIs
- **Request success rate** (non-5xx)
- **End-to-end latency percentiles** (p50 / p95 / p99)
- **Streaming reliability** (disconnect/error events)

### Exclusions (high-level)
Exclusions are standardized in the SLI spec and SLO definitions pages, but at a minimum this program explicitly addresses:
- Filtering invalid requests (4xx validation) and rate-limited requests (429) from “service reliability” accounting.
- Rules for client aborts vs server disconnects for streaming.
- Retry and fallback accounting rules (to avoid double-counting while preserving user-perceived reliability).

---

## Out of scope (Q1 2026)
- Contract changes for Private / on-prem.
- Per-model SLO commitments (we will expose “top contributors” without committing to per-model SLOs).
- Unlimited cardinality breakouts (per-customer/per-model/per-route everywhere). Where needed, we will add controlled breakdowns with strict guardrails.

Contract changes for Private / on-prem.
- Per-model SLO commitments (we will expose “top contributors” without committing to per-model SLOs).
- Unlimited cardinality breakouts (per-customer/per-model/per-route everywhere). Where needed, we will add controlled breakdowns with strict guardrails.

---

## Guiding principles
- **One set of canonical definitions.** There must be a single source of truth for “success,” “latency,” and “streaming failure.”
- **Tier tags at ingest, preserved through routing.** Tier labeling must be correct at ingress and propagated across retries/fallback.
- **Budgets drive behavior.** Error budgets are not passive reporting; they gate risk (with phased enforcement).
- **Graceful degradation is a feature, not an accident.** Fallback and overload shedding must be intentional and consistently accounted for.
- **Gradual enforcement.** Warn-only → soft gates → hard gates, with an emergency fix path.

---

## Deliverables
### Documentation (Confluence)
- Tiered SLO definitions and SLI formulas (Hosted vs Dedicated)
- Error budget policy and enforcement rules
- Observability SLI specification for gateway/routing
- Runbooks and incident process updates

### Engineering assets
- Tier-aware SLI metrics and event taxonomy
- SLO config schema + validation tooling
- Error budget computation pipeline (rolling windows) + data quality checks
- Dashboards + burn-rate alerts
- CI/CD deploy gates (warn-only then enforced)

### Customer-facing alignment artifacts
- SLO → SLA mapping and exclusion alignment
- Tier-specific escalation expectations for CS/SE
- (Dedicated) customer SLO reporting view and access model

---

## Milestones and timeline (Q1 2026)
This is a quarter-scale rollout. Dates are targets; execution uses Linear tickets referenced from the program board.

### Phase 1 — Discovery + SLI definitions (2–3 weeks)
**Outcome:** Agreement on measurement boundaries and canonical event/metric definitions.
- Finalize SLIs: success/error semantics, latency measurement points, streaming rules, exclusions.
- Validate tier labeling approach and propagation rules.
- Identify data quality gaps (missing tags, inconsistent status codes, incomplete streaming events).

### Phase 2 — SLO target proposal + review (2 weeks)
**Outcome:** Signed-off tier-specific SLO targets per endpoint class and region.
- Produce target matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated by endpoint (chat/completions, embeddings, streaming).
- Review feasibility with Infra (capacity headroom) and Routing (fallback behavior).
- Product approval and documentation of rationale and trade-offs.

### Phase 3 — Implementation (3–5 weeks)
**Outcome:** Dashboards, alerting, and budget computation live; initial policy hooks in CI.
- Dashboards: per-tier and regional views, “top contributors,” links to traces/logs.
- Multi-window burn-rate alerts + paging policy (severity mapping).
- Budget calculation job (rolling windows), backfill approach, and data quality checks.
- Deploy gate (warn-only) tied to budget burn state.

### Phase 4 — Rollout + training (2 weeks)
**Outcome:** Operationalized program across on-call, CS/SE, and Product.

## Enforcement model (phased)
This program intentionally stages enforcement to avoid blocking critical reliability fixes early on.

1) **Visibility first** (dashboards + annotations)
- SLO dashboards available for Hosted and Dedicated.
- Deploy and incident annotations visible on SLO timelines.

2) **Alerting** (multi-window burn-rate)
- Burn-rate alerts page correct rotations.
- Alerts link directly to dashboards, traces, and mitigation runbooks.

3) **Warn-only gates**
- CI/CD checks evaluate current error budget state.
- Gate posts warnings (Slack + deploy output) and logs any overrides.

4) **Enforced gates**
- When a tier is in a red state (budget exhausted or acute burn), block non-emergency deploys.
- Emergency fixes permitted via explicit override procedure with audit trail.

---

## Graceful degradation (expectations by tier)
We will document tier-specific behavior and ensure SLI accounting aligns with user impact.

**Hosted (shared):**
- Prefer platform stability under overload: bounded queues, overload shedding, and controlled fallback to compatible variants.
- Expect more aggressive protective measures (rate limiting, load shedding) to protect shared infrastructure.

**Dedicated:**
- Prioritize predictability: capacity headroom commitments, fast mitigation via fleet actions, and conservative fallback policies.

Title: Tiered SLOs + Error Budget Program (Q1 2026)
Source: EnterpriseRAG/confluence
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/tiered-slo-and-error-budget-program-q1-2026.json
Connector: confluence
Workspace: eng-sre

Expect more aggressive protective measures (rate limiting, load shedding) to protect shared infrastructure.

**Dedicated:**
- Prioritize predictability: capacity headroom commitments, fast mitigation via fleet actions, and conservative fallback policies.
- Customer-specific dashboards and incident comms should reflect dedicated impact separately from Hosted.

> Important: Fallback/retry behavior must not “hide” failures by shifting the user-visible failure mode. Accounting will follow the SLI spec (including how retries are deduplicated and how final user outcome is counted).

---

## Success metrics
### Reliability outcomes (measurable)
- Tiered SLO dashboards show stable data coverage (no major metric gaps) across in-scope regions.
- Burn-rate alerts have an acceptable signal-to-noise ratio (tracked by SRE):
  - < 15% alerts classified as “actionless / data issue” after tuning period.
- Reduced recurrence of top customer escalations:
  - Fewer P0/P1 escalations due to latency spikes and streaming disconnect ambiguity.

### Operational outcomes
- On-call can execute a consistent playbook for budget burn (traffic shaping, fallback policy adjustments, capacity actions, rollbacks).
- Release risk is explicitly managed:
  - When budget is constrained, risky rollouts are deferred or require higher scrutiny.

### Org / alignment outcomes
- Product SLA language and internal SLO measurement are aligned (documented mapping exists, with clear exclusions).
- CS/SE have an intake + escalation workflow tied to tiers and dashboards.

---

## Risks and mitigations
- **Risk: Metric cardinality explosion** (per-model/per-customer labels in hot-path metrics).
  - Mitigation: strict label allowlist; “top-N contributors” computed in controlled pipelines; dedicated account dashboards use scoped access and pre-aggregation.

- **Risk: Incorrect tier labeling** leading to invalid SLO reporting.
  - Mitigation: enforce tagging at ingress; add propagation tests; compare tag coverage in telemetry validation job; block rollout if tag coverage falls below threshold.",
